paragraphs.text: At the corner of the cemetery fence stands the four-foot whitewashed Sohon Kanuva boundary stone. Squatting atop the narrow masonry pillar—yet towering sixteen feet into the night—is a colossal form plastered in grey human ash, its left shoulder stove inward from the warrior Gothaimbara's kick, crowned with the wet, tusked head of a wild boar.
In its right fist it squeezes a pale ash-gourd shaped like a human torso, drinking the red lime-sap that runs between its knuckles. The air turns thick with dummala smoke as

paragraphs.text: A silent, concussive shockwave—the Charnel Gassīma—detonates at the base of your skull and rips down your vertebrae. The horizon of the tank bund tilts forty-five degrees into the black water, and every night-insect in Anuradhapura goes simultaneously mute. Behind your left scapula, the night air congeals into freezing tallow:

paragraphs.text: The moonless sky above the tank bund drops like a quarry slab. Before your lungs can draw air, a freezing, sledgehammer blow slams squarely between your shoulder blades—not the strike of knuckles, but the impact of a wet sack of cemetery ash dropped from thirty feet overhead.

You pitch face-first into the red gravel beside the twisted bicycle frame. Your cervical spine locks solid, your teeth chatter until the enamel chips, and the boar-headed shadow blots out the stars above your back:

paragraphs.wakingText: You merely struck your shoulder against the iron handlebar
paragraphs.corruptedText: My five fingers are branded in indelible charnel soot across your flesh!

paragraphs.text: The cold steel of the Giraya betel-cutter bites into your palm, grounding the shockwave before it can enter your heart. A furious, guttural boar-snort shears a branch from the overhanging banyan tree, pelting the gravel with dry twigs, before retreating into the cemetery mist as the temple bell tolls for the Aluya dawn watch.
When you wheel your bent bicycle into your compound at daybreak, the back of your white cotton shirt is scorched with a five-fingered print of grey ash—yet the skin beneath is unmarked.

When your elders cut away your torn shirt, a stark, five-fingered handprint of greasy black cremation soot—the Anguru Atha—is stamped deep into the flesh over your left shoulder blade. Whether struck by the headless duelist avatar Jayasena Yaka or the boar-snouted Maha Sohona, whispered prayers alone will fail. In the therapeutic psychodrama of the Thovil, the paralyzed victim must hear the entire village laugh aloud at the demon's humiliation until his mortal terror shatters.

paragraphs.text: The yak bera drums pivot from a funeral thunder into a sharp, syncopated comic banter. Wearing the bristling wild-boar mask of Mahasona, your dancer lumbers into the sand arena roaring for raw human blood—only for the drummer to mock his backwards-turned neck and challenge him to a rigged game of cards (Kola Sellama) for stale rice-cakes.

To strip the titan of his terror and unlock the boy's spine, you must win three consecutive comic trumps on the mat—answering his Boar, Charnel Ash, and Crossroads boasts with Gothaimbara's Little Toe, the Iron Giraya, and the Dawn Rooster's Crow—and then hurl the Pandama torch upward against his wind to ignite the Dummala fire-cloud.

paragraphs.text: A blinding mushroom of powdered Dummala resin fire roars twenty feet into the Anuradhapura night! Outlined against the rolling orange fireball, the boar-headed shadow trips over the edge of the card mat as the watching villagers—and the shivering boy on the verandah—erupt into cathartic, fearless laughter.

You step barefoot onto the wet inner courtyard sand. One by one, the four earthen boundary lamps around your compound perimeter are being snuffed out from the outside:
To the West, bruised Nil Manel petals float in the rain-gutter; to the North-East, a wet white saree hem drags across the culvert grate; to the South, a macaque-jawed shadow chatters on the well-wall; and by the northern gate, a twelve-cubit boar silhouette breathes grey steam over the hedge.

paragraphs.text: Inside the shuttered shrine room, the brass Pahana flame burns a sickly, eclipsed violet. On the floor before the altar lies a consecrated white ash-gourd—the Alu Puhul—smeared with vermilion lime-paste beside your heavy iron Giraya cutter.

Around the room, the four relics of your past exorcisms begin to bleed: water-lily silt oozes from the clay shards, white Kaduru latex drips from the three masks, red Rathu Kaha Diya pools under the rush mat, and five black soot-fingers smoke on the wall.
